def _prune_packet_intra(packet: DirectivePacket, budget_chars: int) -> DirectivePacket:
    """Prune individual SOFT directives within a packet."""
    if packet.constraint_class == "HARD" or len(packet.text) <= budget_chars:
        return packet
        
    # Split into individual directives
    directives = _parse_packet_directives(packet.text)
    
    # Classify each directive as HARD or SOFT
    classified = []
    for directive in directives:
        text = directive["text"]
        is_hard = (
            packet.constraint_class == "HARD" or
            any(marker in text.upper() for marker in ["MUST", "SHALL", "REQUIRED", "NEVER"]) or
            "HARD" in text.upper()
        )
        classified.append({
            "text": text,
            "hard": is_hard,
            "original_index": directive["index"]
        })
    
    # Start with all HARD directives
    kept = [d for d in classified if d["hard"]]
    kept_indices = {d["original_index"] for d in kept}
    
    # Add SOFT directives in priority order until budget
    soft_directives = [d for d in classified if not d["hard"]]
    
    # Priority: earlier directives (likely more important)
    soft_directives.sort(key=lambda x: x["original_index"])
    
    current_chars = sum(len(d["text"]) for d in kept)
    
    for directive in soft_directives:
        if current_chars + len(directive["text"]) <= budget_chars:
            kept.append(directive)
            kept_indices.add(directive["original_index"])
            current_chars += len(directive["text"])
        else:
            break
    
    # Reconstruct packet text
    kept.sort(key=lambda x: x["original_index"])
    
    # Group by original sections
    sections = []
    current_section = []
    for directive in kept:
        text = directive["text"]
        # Check if this starts a new section
        if text.strip().startswith(("#", "===")) and current_section:
            sections.append("\n".join(current_section))
            current_section = [text]
        else:
            current_section.append(text)
    
    if current_section:
        sections.append("\n".join(current_section))
    
    pruned_text = "\n\n".join(sections)
    
    # Create new packet
    return DirectivePacket(
        layer=packet.layer,
        name=packet.name + "_pruned",
        text=pruned_text,
        constraint_class=packet.constraint_class,
        domain=packet.domain,
        model=packet.model,
        tags=packet.tags.union({"intra_pruned"})
    )

def _parse_packet_directives(text: str) -> list[dict]:
    """Parse packet text into individual directives."""
    lines = text.split("\n")
    directives = []
    current_directive = []
    directive_index = 0
    
    for line in lines:
        stripped = line.strip()
        
        # Start new directive on section breaks or bullet points
        if (stripped.startswith(("#", "===", "---")) or
            stripped.startswith(("- ", "* ", "• ", "1.", "2.", "a)", "b)")) or
            (current_directive and stripped == "")):
            
            if current_directive:
                directives.append({
                    "text": "\n".join(current_directive).strip(),
                    "index": directive_index
                })
                directive_index += 1
                current_directive = []
            
            if stripped:
                current_directive.append(line)
        elif stripped or current_directive:  # Non-empty line or continuing directive
            current_directive.append(line)
    
    # Add last directive
    if current_directive:
        directives.append({
            "text": "\n".join(current_directive).strip(),
            "index": directive_index
        })
    
    return directives

            if norm and norm not in seen and len(norm) > 10:  # Ignore very short lines

        text = "\n".join(deduped)

    # Enforce max length (with priority preservation)

@dataclass
class DirectiveConflict:
    """Record of a resolved conflict."""
    directive_a: str
    layer_a: str
    directive_b: str
    layer_b: str
    resolution: str
    winner: str

def _resolve_layer_conflicts(composed_set: ComposedDirectiveSet) -> tuple[ComposedDirectiveSet, list[DirectiveConflict]]:
    """Resolve conflicts between directive layers."""
    conflicts = []
    
    # Extract directives with layer and hardness
    all_directives = []
    for packet in composed_set.packets:
        directives = _parse_packet_directives(packet.text)
        for d in directives:
            all_directives.append({
                "text": d["text"],
                "layer": packet.layer,
                "hard": packet.constraint_class == "HARD",
                "packet_name": packet.name
            })
    
    # Group similar directives by topic
    topics = {}
    for d in all_directives:
        topic = _extract_directive_topic(d["text"])
        if topic not in topics:
            topics[topic] = []
        topics[topic].append(d)
    
    # Resolve conflicts within each topic
    resolved_directives = []
    for topic, dir_list in topics.items():
        if len(dir_list) <= 1:
            resolved_directives.extend(dir_list)
            continue
            
        # Sort by priority: HARD > SOFT, universal > domain > phenotype > situation
        dir_list.sort(key=lambda x: (
            not x["hard"],  # HARD first
            {"universal": 0, "domain": 1, "phenotype": 2, "situation": 3}[x["layer"]]
        ))
        
        winner = dir_list[0]
        resolved_directives.append(winner)
        
        # Record conflicts
        for other in dir_list[1:]:
            if _directives_conflict(winner["text"], other["text"]):
                conflicts.append(DirectiveConflict(
                    directive_a=winner["text"][:100],
                    layer_a=winner["layer"],
                    directive_b=other["text"][:100],
                    layer_b=other["layer"],
                    resolution=f"{winner['layer']} wins over {other['layer']}",
                    winner=winner["packet_name"]
                ))
    
    # Reconstruct packets with resolved directives
    # Group by original packets
    packet_map = {}
    for d in resolved_directives:
        key = (d["layer"], d["packet_name"])
        if key not in packet_map:
            packet_map[key] = []
        packet_map[key].append(d["text"])
    
    # Update packets
    new_packets = []
    for packet in composed_set.packets:
        key = (packet.layer, packet.name)
        if key in packet_map:
            new_text = "\n\n".join(packet_map[key])
            new_packet = DirectivePacket(
                layer=packet.layer,
                name=packet.name + "_resolved",
                text=new_text,
                constraint_class=packet.constraint_class,
                domain=packet.domain,
                model=packet.model,
                tags=packet.tags.union({"conflict_resolved"})
            )
            new_packets.append(new_packet)
        else:
            new_packets.append(packet)
    
    # Update composed set
    new_rendered = _render_directive_text(new_packets)
    
    return ComposedDirectiveSet(
        packets=new_packets,
        rendered_text=new_rendered,
        policy=composed_set.policy,
        cid=composed_set.cid + "_resolved",
        constraint_count=composed_set.constraint_count,
        token_estimate=composed_set.token_estimate,
        constraint_density=composed_set.constraint_density,
        coherence_budget=composed_set.coherence_budget,
        pruned_soft=composed_set.pruned_soft,
        manifest={**composed_set.manifest, "conflicts_resolved": len(conflicts)}
    ), conflicts

def _extract_directive_topic(text: str) -> str:
    """Extract the main topic of a directive."""
    text_lower = text.lower()
    
    # Keyword mapping to topics
    topic_map = [
        ("format", ["format", "style", "language", "concise", "detailed"]),
        ("verification", ["verify", "check", "test", "validate"]),
        ("falsification", ["falsify", "counterexample", "refute"]),
        ("constraints", ["constraint", "must", "shall", "require"]),
        ("output", ["output", "respond", "answer", "return"]),
        ("behavior", ["behavior", "act", "do not", "avoid"]),
    ]
    
    for topic, keywords in topic_map:
        if any(keyword in text_lower for keyword in keywords):
            return topic
    
    return "general"

def _directives_conflict(a: str, b: str) -> bool:
    """Determine if two directives conflict."""
    a_lower = a.lower()
    b_lower = b.lower()
    
    # Check for opposite instructions
    opposites = [
        ("detailed", "concise"),
        ("complex", "simple"),
        ("long", "short"),
        ("many", "few"),
        ("always", "never"),
        ("must", "should not"),
        ("require", "avoid"),
    ]
    
    for term1, term2 in opposites:
        if (term1 in a_lower and term2 in b_lower) or (term2 in a_lower and term1 in b_lower):
            return True
    
    return False

# Update compose() function to call resolver
def compose_with_resolution(**kwargs) -> tuple[ComposedDirectiveSet, list[DirectiveConflict]]:
    """Compose with conflict resolution."""
    composed = compose(**kwargs)
    return _resolve_layer_conflicts(composed)

import numpy as np

@dataclass
class ExperimentLog:
    model: str
    directive_chars: int
    response_chars: int
    elapsed_s: float
    findings: List[str]
    quality_score: float  # 0-1, from manual grading
    
def calibrate_coherence_thresholds(log_files: List[Path]) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """Calibrate optimal coherence thresholds from experiment logs."""
    
    # Parse logs
    experiments = []
    for log_file in log_files:
        with open(log_file, 'r') as f:
            data = json.load(f)
            exp = ExperimentLog(
                model=data["model"],
                directive_chars=data.get("directive_length", 0),
                response_chars=len(data.get("response", "")),
                elapsed_s=data.get("elapsed_s", 0),
                findings=data.get("findings", []),
                quality_score=data.get("quality_score", 0.5)
            )
            experiments.append(exp)
    
    # Group by model
    by_model = {}
    for exp in experiments:
        if exp.model not in by_model:
            by_model[exp.model] = []
        by_model[exp.model].append(exp)
    
    # Calculate optimal threshold per model
    thresholds = {}
    
    for model, exps in by_model.items():
        if len(exps) < 3:
            thresholds[model] = DEFAULT_COHERENCE_BUDGET
            continue
        
        # Calculate metrics for each experiment
        metrics = []
        for exp in exps:
            # Estimate tokens (chars/4)
            directive_tokens = max(exp.directive_chars // 4, 1)
            response_tokens = max(exp.response_chars // 4, 1)
            
            # Constraint count from directive (rough estimate: 1 per 200 chars)
            constraint_count = max(exp.directive_chars // 200, 1)
            
            # Density
            density = constraint_count / directive_tokens
            
            # Finding quality metric: findings per 1000 tokens, weighted by quality score
            findings_per_k = (len(exp.findings) * 1000) / response_tokens if response_tokens > 0 else 0
            weighted_quality = findings_per_k * exp.quality_score
            
            metrics.append({
                "density": density,
                "findings_per_k": findings_per_k,
                "weighted_quality": weighted_quality,
                "directive_chars": exp.directive_chars
            })
        
        # Sort by density
        metrics.sort(key=lambda x: x["density"])
        
        # Find peak quality
        peak_quality = max(m["weighted_quality"] for m in metrics)
        
        # Find density where quality drops below 90% of peak
        optimal_threshold = DEFAULT_COHERENCE_BUDGET
        
        for i in range(len(metrics)):
            if metrics[i]["weighted_quality"] >= 0.9 * peak_quality:
                # Look ahead for drop
                for j in range(i, len(metrics)):
                    if metrics[j]["weighted_quality"] < 0.9 * peak_quality:
                        # Threshold is midpoint between last good and first bad
                        if j > 0:
                            optimal_threshold = (metrics[j-1]["density"] + metrics[j]["density"]) / 2
                        else:
                            optimal_threshold = metrics[0]["density"]
                        break
                else:
                    # No drop found, use max density
                    optimal_threshold = metrics[-1]["density"]
                break
        
        # Cap thresholds to reasonable range
        optimal_threshold = max(0.005, min(optimal_threshold, 0.03))
        thresholds[model] = round(optimal_threshold, 4)
    
    return thresholds

def update_model_budgets_from_calibration(log_dir: Path):
    """Update MODEL_COHERENCE_BUDGETS from calibration."""
    log_files = list(log_dir.glob("experiment_*.json"))
    if not log_files:
        return
    
    thresholds = calibrate_coherence_thresholds(log_files)
    
    # Update global variable
    global MODEL_COHERENCE_BUDGETS
    for model, threshold in thresholds.items():
        if model in MODEL_COHERENCE_BUDGETS:
            MODEL_COHERENCE_BUDGETS[model] = threshold
        else:
            # Add new model entry
            MODEL_COHERENCE_BUDGETS[model] = threshold
    
    # Log the updates
    print(f"Updated coherence budgets from calibration:")
    for model, budget in MODEL_COHERENCE_BUDGETS.items():
        print(f"  {model}: {budget}")
